title: ATAN2 18 of 18 at build 20026 - what was counted is the #NUM! boundary

upstream_anchor.section: XMD-007 - ATAN2 -> #NUM! when the y/x ratio overflows

status_plain: Excel returns #NUM! from ATAN2 exactly when x is nonzero and the implicit y/x ratio overflows to infinity - ATAN2(1e-200,1e108) is finite, ATAN2(1e-200,1e109) is #NUM! - while the axis case x = 0 stays valid. The four-quadrant angle is finite everywhere off the origin, so this is Excel forming the ratio first and inheriting its overflow; a two-argument atan2 would never do it. OxFunc reproduces the departure deliberately: atan2_kernel guards x != 0 && (y/x).is_infinite() -> #NUM!. The evidence line reads "live Excel 16.0 build 20026 (18/18 bit-exact)" - the build is restated on the same line as the figure, which is rare in this evidence base. The ambiguity that must ride along: the entry is about an ERROR-PLACEMENT boundary and the phrase used is "bit-exact". This record publishes the weaker reading - the boundary was measured, not the angle - and carries the count on the numeric axis only because the Excel-math-deviation catalogue is a numeric register by the Handbook's own axis rule.
